_comment: WC2026 ROUND OF 16 (bracket tie 96: winner of Switzerland-Algeria vs winner of Colombia-Ghana) -- the LAST R16 tie. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets Argentina (who came from 2-0 down to beat Egypt) in the quarter-finals (QF100). Routes: Switzerland WON Group B (1-1 Qatar, 4-1 Bosnia, 2-1 Canada; 7 pts, GF 7 GA 3, rating 81) -- balanced and attacking (7 goals) but not airtight (GA 3) -- then beat Algeria 2-0 in the R32 (clean sheet). Colombia WON Group K (3-1 Uzbekistan, 1-0 DR Congo, 0-0 Portugal; 7 pts, GF 4 GA 1, rating 83) -- organized, defensively strong (GA 1, HELD Portugal 0-0) -- then beat Ghana 1-0 in the R32 (controlled, clean sheet). Class gap is TINY (~2, 83 vs 81) -> essentially a COIN-FLIP; Colombia the marginal favourite by rating + defensive solidity, despite Switzerland's nominal home. KEY texture: both are competent with decent-to-good defences (Colombia especially -- GA 1, held Portugal; Switzerland kept a clean sheet vs Algeria) and neither is a shootout side -> a TIGHT, low-to-moderate-scoring tie (1-1/0-0/1-0 shape) with VERY HIGH extra-time/penalty risk (near-even + low-scoring = the lottery zone). BTTS kept NEAR-NEUTRAL / slight-No (49.5%): both can score but both defend, not forced either way. RECAL: first pass (SUI 1.25 / COL 1.15) sat 3.0 pts ABOVE the market on Switzerland (37.6 vs 34.6) -- over-crediting the nominal home edge (the recurring Canada-Morocco / USA-Belgium error); trimmed SUI 1.25 -> 1.18 and lifted COL 1.15 -> 1.20 to align, making Colombia the marginal favourite the market sees. Home = Switzerland (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.result: Switzerland 0-0 Colombia (after extra time), Switzerland won on PENALTIES. Switzerland advance to the quarter-finals (where they meet Argentina). The tightest possible tie went the full distance to the shootout.

_postmatch.verdict: Textbook TEXTURE hit -- as good as a coin-flip tie gets. I called this a dead coin-flip (LOW, 'no strong read') between two competent, well-defended sides, with a TIGHT, low-scoring shape (total 2.38, Under lean, top scorelines 1-1/0-0/1-0) and the round's VERY HIGH extra-time/penalty risk (ET 29.9%, pens 16.1%). Result: 0-0 through 90' and extra time, decided on PENALTIES -- the model's central scenario landing almost exactly (0-0 was a top-2 scoreline at 10.3%; the low total + two good defences + near-even sides pointed straight at the lottery). The advancement split was 50.6/49.4 -- a genuine coin-flip -- and Switzerland (the marginal 49.4% underdog) won the near-random shootout. That is the process working: a 50/50 that flags 'likely to go deep' and then goes to penalties, with the winner decided by the coin-flip, is a hit, not a miss -- exactly as with Australia-Egypt (Egypt won its shootout) and the reverse of Germany/Netherlands (favourites who LOST theirs, graded 🟡). Here the sides were so even that either result is fully within the forecast.
_postmatch.lesson: The 'two competent, well-defended, near-even sides' profile is the penalty-lottery zone -- correctly flagged (highest pens% of the R16 alongside the tight ties) and it delivered a 0-0 shootout. When the model has NO strong read (LOW, ~50/50), the honest deliverable IS 'this is a coin-flip that will likely go deep', and the advancement split (49/51) is the content, not a confident pick. Switzerland winning the shootout from the marginal-underdog side is the near-random lottery resolving -- not a process error; the low-scoring, deep-tie TEXTURE was the real, and correct, call. Also validated again: aligning OFF the over-credited nominal home edge (I trimmed Switzerland to make Colombia the marginal favourite) was right on the 1X2 -- the tie was dead even, exactly as re-priced.
